proved_claims.statement: Every binary linear interval-constraint family with integer bounds has a consecutive set of attainable ranks, including after coordinate conditioning.
proved_claims.proof: REPORT.md: coordinatewise floor of a convex interpolation of feasible prefix-height vectors.

proved_claims.statement: If q*c_q >= (q+1)*c_(q-1) for every symmetric linear interval-band family on 2q coordinates and every q>=1, then every binary linear interval-constraint family has an ultra-log-concave weighted rank sequence of order its number of variables for every nonnegative position-weight vector.

For every m<=9, every collection of integer lower and upper bounds on sums over linear intervals in {1,...,m}, and every nonnegative real position-weight vector, the weighted feasible-word rank sequence is ULC of order m.
proved_claims.evidence: Complete enumeration of symmetric interval-band families in even dimensions 2,4,6,8; exactly 2,16,377,32554 nonempty families; no APP defect.

proved_claims.statement: For arbitrary m and every linear interval-constraint family and nonnegative weights, k*(m-k)*f_k^2 >= (k+1)*(m-k+1)*f_(k-1)*f_(k+1) at k in {1,2,3,4,m-4,m-3,m-2,m-1} intersect {1,...,m-1}.
For every m>=0, every laminar collection of constrained intervals with integer rank bounds, and every nonnegative position-weight vector, the weighted feasible-word rank sequence is ULC of order m.

open_questions.statement: For every integer q>=1 and every collection of integer bandwidths B_I>=0 on linear intervals I of {1,...,2q}, let H={x in {0,1}^{2q}: abs(2*sum_(i in I)x_i-|I|)<=B_I for all I}, and c_j=number of x in H with sum_i x_i=j. Is q*c_q >= (q+1)*c_(q-1)?
open_questions.evidence: Exhaustive verification for q<=4. Bandwidth parity may be rounded down to that of |I|; negative bandwidths give an empty family. Laminar systems follow from closure arguments. No all-q proof.
open_questions.implication: An affirmative answer proves arbitrary weighted ULC of order m for every linear interval-constraint family.

open_questions.statement: For every graph G equal to a path or a cycle on n vertices and every integer ell>=1, is (gamma_k(G^ell)/binom(n,k))_(k=0)^n log-concave?
open_questions.new_scope: All weighted path-power families for n<=9 and endpoint indices within four of either end for arbitrary n. Laminar interval families all dimensions. General crossing-neighborhood and cycle cases not closed.

obstructions.statement_refuted: In every symmetric interval family on 2q coordinates, every feasible rank q-1 word has a feasible rank q superset obtained by changing one zero to one.
obstructions.witness: q=3, pair equations x1+x2=x2+x3=x4+x5=x5+x6=1; rank2 word 010010 has no feasible rank3 superset; the two central words are 010101 and101010.

obstructions.statement_refuted: The normalized central ULC defect is coefficientwise nonnegative in independent position weights for every interval family.
obstructions.witness: Unrestricted m=2: f1^2-4*f0*f2 = w1^2-2*w1*w2+w2^2; mixed coefficient -2.
obstructions.numerical_property_survives: Defect equals (w1-w2)^2 and is nonnegative for every real weight vector.
